name: Act 1 (Ogham)
summary: First PoE2 act, in the forests of Ogham and Clearfell. The Exile escapes execution, helps Una and Renly, frees the Hooded One, and ends by defeating Count Geonor; the Seed of Corruption flees east with the Countess.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_1", "locator": "intro + Progression"}]

name: Act 2 (Vastiri)
summary: Second PoE2 act, in the Vastiri Desert and Keth. The Exile joins the Ardura Maraketh caravan, recreates the Horn of the Vastiri to dispel Jamanra's sandstorm, pursues the Countess to the Dreadnought, and learns the Hooded One is Sin.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_2", "locator": "intro + Progression"}]

name: Act 3 (Utzaal)
summary: Third PoE2 act, in the jungles and drowned city of Utzaal. The Exile lowers the lake, enters the Vaal sites, is sent back in time via a gateway to Utzaal's past, and brings Doryani to the present.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_3", "locator": "intro + Progression"}]

name: Act 4 (Ngamakanui)
summary: Fourth act of Path of Exile 2 (added in 0.3.0 The Third Edict). The Exile, the Hooded One and Doryani sail from Kingsmarch around the Karui archipelago Ngamakanui to recover three Precursor weapon pieces, find a forge, and reforge the Weapon meant to destroy the Beast, clashing with the Twilight Order and the Tukohama chieftain Tavakai.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "intro + Progression"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "quest summary"}]

name: Act 5 (Oriath)
summary: Announced/datamined fifth act, not released as of 2026-11-05 (planned for the 1.0 release, 2026-12-11). Wiki text: set in Oriath, secretly rebuilt by the Twilight Order after Sirus destroyed it, where the player arrives in search of the Beast. Datamined listings name Slums, Grand Arena, Gardens, Den of Pleasure, Pantheon of the Forsaken Gods and bosses incl. Lumerius and the Countess; treat all details as unconfirmed.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_5", "locator": "intro text"}, {"source_id": "src_web_poe2db_act5", "locator": "area/boss/quest lists (datamine)"}, {"source_id": "src_web_allthings_poe2_release", "locator": "1.0 release date and Acts 5-6 confirmed"}]

name: Act 6 (final act)
summary: Announced sixth and final act of the PoE2 campaign, not released as of 2026-11-05. The PoE2 wiki only calls it the 'sixth and final storyline act'; no story content is confirmed. Rumours of its setting (e.g. inside the Beast) are unverified fan speculation.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_6", "locator": "intro text"}, {"source_id": "src_web_allthings_poe2_release", "locator": "Acts 5-6 complete the campaign at 1.0"}]

name: Epilogue / Endgame (Legacy of the Precursors)
summary: Endgame container (0.5.0) opened when the attempt to sail on Oriath ends at the Ziggurat Refuge: the Hooded One sleeps in corruption, Doryani builds a Waygate and the hunt for the Edicts begins. Distinct from PoE1's Epilogue.

name: Interlude 1: Curse of Holten (Ezomytes)
summary: First Interlude after Act 4: the Hooded One takes the Exile to Ogham where Renly's Ezomytes are being abducted by Thane Wulfric and Lady Elswyth of Holten. Defeating them wins the Ezomytes for the war on Oriath. GGG reportedly intends Interludes to go away when Acts 5-6 arrive (non-canon status unverified).

name: Map Device
summary: Ancient device of golden instruments that opens portals to the worlds of the Atlas. Per Valdo's Book of Memories it was built by the Watchers of Decay to travel to and lock the Elder's dreamland; Templar expeditions under High Templar Venarius found a broken one in Wraeclast's ruins and Valdo Caeserius (with the Shade's help) assembled it in the Oriath academy. Zana later found another in ruined Oriath; in the legacy epilogue Kirac rebuilt one from parts in the Vault of Venarius; Isla later reimagined it with Kalguuran runes. Different peoples are said to have built their own versions. No source in the corpus ties it to the Precursors.

sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Doryani: 'The machine you see here... I call it... a Waygate. Using the leylines, the Waygate can take us anywhere they reach.'"}]

name: Waystone

sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Doryani: 'Take this Waystone. Mark your desired coordinates on it. Place it in the Waygate.'"}]

name: The Atlas of Worlds (concept)
summary: The endgame structure of PoE1: a web of alternate worlds ('maps') reached through the Map Device. Wiki lore says it was either found or created by the Elder as a hunting ground; after the Elder's defeat other powers (Maven, Eldritch Horrors, the Originator) contest it. PoE2 has its own, separate Atlas whose Precursor Towers are mentioned in PoE1 wiki lore.

name: Cataclysm
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "from the Precursor era to c. 1339 IC (several events)", "story_order": null}
summary: Lore term for the world-ending catastrophes that destroyed civilisations: the unknown cataclysm that wiped out the Precursors, the Vaal Cataclysm (also 'The Fall', c. 400 BIC), and the Eternal Empire Cataclysm (~1339 IC). The corpus uses the word for each event but does not define a single in-world category; this node groups those uses. Not the PoE2 epilogue quest 'Cataclysm's Wake', which is an Atlas tutorial quest.

name: Citadels (Iron, Copper, Stone)
summary: Three Atlas fortresses (Iron, Copper, Stone) whose bosses drop one Crisis Fragment each toward the Arbiter of Ash: Iron Citadel = Count Geonor, Copper Citadel = Jamanra, Stone Citadel = Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge (agreed by several guides; the poe2 wiki Doryani page also lists the Stone Citadel). The removed 0.1-0.4 epilogue quests Faridun Foray (boss listed Count Geonor), Ezomyte Infiltration (boss listed The Perennial King) and Vaal Incursion (boss Doryani) all start 'Investigate the Burning Monolith'; how The Perennial King maps to Jamanra is unclear. Fragment mapping differs between guides.

summary: Lore force of mutation and malformation tied to the Beast and its predecessors: the Beast 'possesses corrupting powers' that mutate whatever contacts it; Kitava is called 'God of Corruption' in Karui dialogue; Precursors mastered corruption and Doryani attempts to harness the Precursor Weapon to destroy corruption. Not the Corrupted-item mechanic.

name: Crisis Fragments
summary: Fragments needed to open the sealed door of the Burning Monolith (Arbiter of Ash). In 0.1-0.4 three were needed (Ancient, Weathered, Faded), one per Citadel boss. In the 0.5 quest log only the Ancient and Weathered fragments are picked up in the Fortress Enigma Chambers; Citadels continue to drop them for repeat runs. Guides disagree on which Citadel drops which (most: Iron=Ancient, Copper=Faded, Stone=Weathered), and the quest log matches that for Geonor (Ancient) and Doryani (Weathered).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_pinnacle_of_flame", "locator": "Obtain three Crisis Fragments"}, {"source_id": "src_web_timesaver_poe2_citadels", "locator": "Citadel-to-Arbiter loop; fragment mapping disagrees between guides"}]

name: Delirium: The Hare and the Raven
summary: 0.5 Delirium storyline ('The Hare and the Raven' in the press release): Elder Madox is freed from a Delirium mirror (Strange Reflection), leads the Exile to the Withered Willow, and the Raven Trickster Tangmazu must be stopped. Official notes: 'An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed, spreading madness across Wraeclast.'
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Delirium (The Hare and the Raven): confrontation with Tangmazu"}, {"source_id": "src_web_domistae_poe2_endgame_guide", "locator": "Delirium"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_strange_reflection", "locator": "Quest log"}, {"source_id": "src_ggg_content_update_0_5_0", "locator": "An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed"}]

name: Doryani's contingencies
summary: Fan-synthesised reading of Doryani's secret preparations: anti-Beast Precursor weapon, flood-sealed Utzaal, and a time gateway needing Vaal blood. Interpretive; some details rest on tertiary YouTube analysis.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_yt_1Zt4tv8fjI4", "locator": "[7:07]-[13:30]"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Doryani dialogue"}]

name: Exile (exile system)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "1599-1600 IC (PoE1); Trarthus precedent c. 870 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: The exile system: criminals of Oriath are sentenced by the Templar government and shipped to Wraeclast. The sentence text reads 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. The player's character is one of these exiles. Precedent exists: under Tyndarus Phrecius, people were exiled to the land later called Trarthus. The wiki gives no single in-world reason for choosing Wraeclast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_letters_of_exile", "locator": "section 'Format' (sentence template); exile entries 1597-1599 IC"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Present'; section 'Reign of Tyndarus Phrecius' (Trarthus exile)"}]

name: Exile's Journey (Day Zero rule)
summary: The wiki's 'Day Zero' rule: each league's narrative starts with the Exile face-down in the sand of the Twilight Strand, having just been exiled by Dominus, so league stories cannot build on earlier leagues' events.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule)"}]

name: Expedition and The Grand Expedition (PoE2)
summary: 0.5 Expedition storyline from Ruins of Kingsmarch: Rog searches for Gwennen across an ocean of islands, Medved, Vorana, Uhtred, Olroth lead factions; a Verisium meteor is the goal.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_grand_expedition", "locator": "quest log"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Expedition: Rog searches for his missing wife, Gwennen"}, {"source_id": "src_web_domistae_poe2_endgame_guide", "locator": "Expedition"}]

name: Ezomyte Runesmithing
summary: Rune craft with Kalguuran origins, revealed by Farrow in 0.5.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Farrow reveals the Kalguuran origins of Ezomyte Runesmithing"}]

name: Nature of godhood (ascension)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "before the creation of the Beast", "story_order": null}
summary: In PoE lore a mortal of rare quality could ascend to godhood on the adoration of their people, shedding mortality; this became impossible once Sin created the Beast. Becoming a god often costs one's humanity. Gods can also be 'made' by belief of followers (Innocence's ascension was fuelled by hatred of Sin).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'Ascension to godhood'"}, {"source_id": "src_ingame_sin_dialogue", "locator": "Sin, 'The Origins of the Gods': \"There was a time before the Beast ... men and women like you could ascend. Through rareness of quality and the adoration of their people...\""}]

name: Eternal calendar
summary: Calendar of 1 IC (Imperialis Conceptus), seven days and thirteen moons (Verusi, Divini, Derivi ... Azmeri).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_calendar_lore", "locator": "days and moons"}, {"source_id": "src_ggg_lore_qa_part_one", "locator": "calendar answer"}]

name: Eternal slave trade
summary: Under Chitus the Empire enslaved Karui, Ezomytes and Maraketh, sending them to mines and cities.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Slave trade'"}]

name: Kalguuran runesmithing
summary: Kalguuran art of engraving starlight runes (Verisium from meteorites) into weapons and armour; Ezomytes learned it from the first expedition; revived as Runesmithing in Settlers and Runeforging in PoE2 Act 4.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "'===Runes==='"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_runeseeker", "locator": "intro"}]

name: Karui Gods
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "ancient; worshipped by the Karui", "story_order": null}
summary: The gods honoured within the Karui Way: Arohongui, Hinekora, Kitava, Ngamahu, Ramako, Tasalio, Tawhoa, Tukohama and Valako, as named on the Karui Gods page.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "intro: 'In the game's lore, The Karui Way has several gods that are representative of or rule over various aspects of the world.'"}]

name: Karui Way (Makanui)
summary: Karui code of honour and traditions (Way of the Warrior); some who follow it forbid virtue gems for causing blood fever.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Karui paragraph 2"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_azmeri", "locator": "Tears of Maji"}]

name: Leylines
summary: Ancient underground structures Doryani believes span the continent beneath the Ziggurat; they power the Waygate and resonate with the Precursor Tower.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Doryani: This Ziggurat was built over what my ancestors called 'leylines'"}]

name: Lord's Trial
summary: Azmerian maze-festival to choose chieftains; raised Veruso to power and inspired Izaro's Labyrinth.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Caspiro'; 'Reign of Izaro'"}]

name: Maraketh Shrine
summary: Room-reward shrines in the PoE2 Trial of the Sekhemas. Each shrine (Tabina, Balbala, Ahkeli or Galai variants) lets the player spend 5 Sacred Water to restore part of their Honour, with a random Boon or Minor Affliction on some variants; the Fountain of Youth minor boon restores 40 Honour when a Maraketh Shrine is venerated.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_maraketh_shrine", "locator": "Full page (stub): 'Maraketh Shrines are found as room rewards in the Trial of the Sekhemas'; shrine list (Honour Tabina / Balbala / Ahkeli / Galai); Fountain of Youth minor boon"}]

name: Martyr of the First Edict (Void league leaderboard)
summary: Rise of the Abyssal mechanic: once per league a level-100 character can be sacrificed at the Site of the Chosen, sending it to the Void league and listing it as the 'Martyr of the First Edict' on the leaderboard. Meta/league flavour; no source explains the naming.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_rise_of_the_abyssal_league", "locator": "Site of the Chosen paragraph"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_league", "locator": "paragraph: 'listed as the Martyr of the First Edict on the leaderboard'"}]

name: Masters of the Atlas
summary: 0.5 storylines of three Atlas Masters: Jado (Order of the Djinn; unlocked by an anomaly map near the start), Hilda (monster hunter, Hilda's Campsite) and Doryani (unlocked by clearing a corruption nexus). The earlier draft's 'ascendancy-like specialisation' claim is unsupported and was removed.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_ggg_content_update_0_5_0", "locator": "Atlas Masters: Jado, Hilda, Doryani; Doryani questline via corruption nexus; Jado via anomaly map"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Atlas Masters"}, {"source_id": "src_web_pcgamesn_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Masters of the Atlas storyline"}]

name: Atlas of Worlds (PoE2)
summary: The PoE2 endgame map network, reached after the campaign via Doryani's Waygate and navigated with Waystones. Rebuilt in 0.5 (Return of the Ancients) with fixed points of interest, storylines and a fully unlockable Atlas passive tree.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest log: 'Use the Map Device and the Waystone to enter a Map'"}, {"source_id": "src_web_pcgamesn_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Atlas passive tree: Fully remade; zone quest chains"}]

name: The Red Pyre
summary: Entity/title in Ailith's Word of the Dreamer ('The Red Pyre burns hot... The Dreamer once knew him, before his addiction'). The fire imagery and the book's subject (the four Breachlords that became Xesht) point to Xoph, Dark Embers; the identification is inferred, not stated.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_word_of_the_dreamer", "locator": "passage on the Red Pyre"}]

name: Rite of the Nameless
summary: Ritual mechanic/quest stage: place the Head of the King on the Incomplete Effigy in Caer Tarth, use it to select five maps, complete Rituals there to collect effigy parts (Tangled Torso, Mossy Arm, Frayed Cloth, Brittle Arm, Ragged Cloth), activate the Effigy and perform the Rite to reach the Darkness and the Bodach. 0.5.5 campaign unique-boss Rituals work similarly.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_maji", "locator": "steps 24-54 (hidden comment block)"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_forbidden_rites", "locator": "unique boss Rituals work similarly to the Rite of the Nameless"}]

name: Ritual (altar mechanic)
summary: Ritual Altars spawn wave encounters inside a ritual circle; defeating monsters earns Favour/Tribute to buy items. PoE1 Ritual league gives no narrative; Vaal Ritual Altars may summon Atziri's Apparition; later Wildwood lore ties 'ritual altars' to the King in the Mists; PoE2 adopts it in Forbidden Rites.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_ritual_league", "locator": "lead paragraph and League mechanic"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_atziri_lore", "locator": "section 'Vaal Ritual Altar'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_forbidden_rites", "locator": "League content"}]

name: Ritual and the King in the Mists (PoE2)
summary: 0.5 Ritual storyline: Aoife, a lost spirit bound by the King in the Mists, appeals to the Wildwood; the prison beneath holds the Bodach; the Rite of the Nameless in Caer Tarth. 0.5.5 adds Ritual altars to every zone.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Ritual: Aoife, a lost spirit, bound by the King in the Mists... Bodach ... Rite of the Nameless"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_forbidden_rites", "locator": "League content"}]

name: Rogue exiles
summary: Exiled criminals who roam Wraeclast as hostile NPCs; originated in Anarchy league (0.11.0), later reused in PoE2 (Lichborn exiles in Rise of the Abyssal).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_anarchy_league", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_rise_of_the_abyssal_league", "locator": "raising a rogue exile as Lichborn"}]

name: Rogue Exiles (PoE2)
summary: Roaming exile NPC bosses introduced in 0.2.0; Abyss can raise a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_dawn_of_the_hunt_league", "locator": "rogue exiles"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_rise_of_the_abyssal_league", "locator": "raising a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile"}]

name: Sekhema
summary: Maraketh leader title; always a woman chosen by merit and anointed with the feather of the Great Roc; tale-women keep the people's history.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Maraketh > Society"}]

name: Thaumaturgy
summary: Gem-based magic whose source is the Beast. Outlawed by Veruso, embraced by Chitus under Malachai's 'Thaumatocracy', and banned again by Voll.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Chitus' and 'Reign of Voll'"}]

name: The Edicts (Precursor murals)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "Precursor age, far older than the Vaal and Winter of the World", "story_order": null}
summary: Series of vague Precursor murals described by the PoE2 wiki as depicting the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it; numbered First to Fourth in game. Known: Third = instrument is the Weapon (Hooded One recognises it as 'the Weapon I saw in that third mural'); Second = Doryani's guess that the Seed was its instrument; Fourth = investigated in the Epilogue after the Arbiter of Ash (PoE1 wiki editors speculate it caused the Great Fire); First = unexplained threat averted in the Epilogue. The full text of the edicts is not given in any source read. Not to be confused with Count Geonor's hanging edicts in Ogham.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "'It was depicted in their Edicts, vague murals that depicts the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'The Third Edict? What is the meaning... of these Edicts?'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural'; Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'"}]

name: Trial of Chaos
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 3 at the Temple of Chaos via an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the quest item Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian). Based on the PoE1 Ultimatum league and overseen by the Trialmaster.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trial_of_chaos", "locator": "section 'Access'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_chaos_lore", "locator": "intro: 'The Trialmaster ... oversee the Trials of Chaos'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trial_of_chaos", "locator": "lead and Access"}]

name: Trial of the Sekhemas
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 2 via the Djinn Barya key (or the quest item Balbala's Barya), a gauntlet of up to 4 floors with bosses including Rattlecage, Hadi and Rafiq, Ashar and Zarokh.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_trial_of_the_sekhemas", "locator": "section 'Access' and floor table"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_trial_of_the_sekhemas", "locator": "lead and Access"}]

name: Utopia (Twilight Order ideal)
summary: The Order's promised god-free world ('without gods... without suffering... without the disease of Divinity'), recruited for with 'Accept Utopia! Embrace the saviour!'. Art book: intention is good but its methods are contentious.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_twilight_order", "locator": "intro quote"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Benedictus / Countess lines"}]

name: Vaal corruption and thaumaturgical technology
summary: Vaal science combined gem-craft, constructs, mechanical technology and corruption drawn from the Beast; much of it was developed by Doryani and housed at Atzoatl and Utzaal. Its influence resurfaces as Vaal side areas, Vaal skill gems and Vaal Orbs in PoE1.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "The Temple of Atzoatl"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_atziri_lore", "locator": "section 'Post Fall'"}]

name: Vaal sacrifice and Vaal souls
summary: Vaal bloodpriests discovered that the souls of the recently killed briefly seek another source of life and can be captured in a vaal skill gem to empower it; human and blood sacrifice powered Vaal constructs and society, and slavery supplied victims.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "History intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_atziri_lore", "locator": "section 'Fall of the Vaal'"}]

name: Verisium
summary: Metal ore found only in fallen meteorites and not native to Wraeclast; Kalguuran runes were typically crafted from it, and in PoE2 Act 4 Dannig forges Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "===Runes===: \"Runes were typically crafted using Verisium, a type of metal ore found only from fallen meteorites, and not native to Wraeclast.\""}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_dark_mists", "locator": "Bring the Verisium to Dannig / Take the Verisium Spikes from Dannig: Dannig crafts Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_runes_of_aldur_league", "locator": "Remnants can contain Verisium used in Runeforging"}, {"source_id": "src_ggg_content_update_0_5_0", "locator": "Seek out the crater of a fallen star, a meteor of pure Verisium"}]

name: Virtue Gems
aliases: ["Tears of Maji", "Tears of the Maji", "Virtue gems"]
summary: Gems from the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy, buried by Veruso and mined by slaves under Chitus; infused into gemlings. Ubiquitous in Vaal society.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_azmeri", "locator": "Culture > Tears of Maji"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Tarcus Veruso'; 'Malachai'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'The Beast'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "History"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Vaal'"}]

name: Humours / Wisps (Wildwood)
summary: In the Viridian Wildwood the four humours (Primal, Vivid, Wild, Sacred) materialise as wisps. The first three share names with Harvest's Primal, Vivid and Wild Lifeforce colours. Sacred humours are harvested by the ritual altars of the King in the Mists.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Viridian Wildwood'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_sacred_grove_quest", "locator": "Walkthrough"}]

name: Hiveborn
summary: Breach-spawn into which the Breachlords were evolving; the Keepers of the Flame, founded through Chayula's dreams, exist to destroy them. The Dreamer is revealed to be of the same kind as the Hiveborn.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_into_the_breach", "locator": "quest steps: Hiveborn invade Wraeclast"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_keepers_league", "locator": "League content"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Hiveborn"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_dreamer", "locator": "Lore: the Breachlords began their evolution into the Hiveborn; the Dreamer is the same creature as the Hiveborn"}]

name: The Lightless (Abyssals)
summary: Ancient subterranean race created, not born, via necromancy, afraid of light; invaded during the Winter of the World and were driven back underground by the returning sun. Antagonists of Abyss and PoE2 Rise of the Abyssals.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lightless", "locator": "intro; Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Winter of the World > The Lightless"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lightless", "locator": "lead and Lore"}]

name: The Nameless
summary: Shadowy beings born with the Wildwood as the 'unseen reflection opposite the mortal world'; led by the King in the Mists; Gruthkul was one.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Viridian Wildwood"}]

name: The Titans
summary: Primordial race that walked molten Wraeclast and inhabited its volcanoes; mostly indifferent to humans; nearly wiped out in the 'rising darkness', with the Molten One the sole survivor.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > The Titans"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_molten_one", "locator": "Lore"}]

name: The Undying
summary: Gemlings and citizens of Sarn transformed by the Cataclysm into mindless monsters that can live for centuries; some gemling legionnaires later regain sentience (Act 8 Grain Gate).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_gemling_legion", "locator": "Maramoa dialogue"}]

name: Vorniculia / horrors
summary: Horror species that attacked Kalguuran outposts; Olroth's Knights culled the Vorniculia.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Colonisation' and 'The Broken Circle'"}]

name: Arakaali, Spinner of Shadows
summary: Vaal spider-goddess of love and death, worshipped by Azmeri artists; consorts with Silk in the Temple of Decay and is killed as Act 7's boss. A relationship with Sin is hinted.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_arakaali_spinner_of_shadows", "locator": "section 'Lore'"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_1E5kADGy5Pw", "locator": "[0:00]-[1:30]"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_arakaali_spinner_of_shadows", "locator": "Act 7 final boss; Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_mother_of_spiders", "locator": "Walkthrough"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "'lesser relationships with ... Arakaali' (cites PoE2 Arakaali's Lust)"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'Arakaali'"}]

name: Arohongui, Daughter of the Moon
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. Daughter of Ramako's alleged impersonator and Sione; lacks the warmth and light of the Sun
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'Karui gods' (Ramako/Arohongui/Rongokurai/Lani Lua/Sione myths)"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui", "locator": "tribe list"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Arohongui/Ramako/Rongokurai paragraph (Karui myth)"}]

name: The Beast
summary: Divine creature, source of thaumaturgy and corruption, grown by Sin from the Dark Ember beneath Highgate to keep the gods asleep. Has no will of its own; exploited by Doryani, Atziri, Chitus, Malachai. The Exile kills it in Act 4; PoE2 follows a new Beast grown from the stolen Seed of Corruption.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_beast_lore", "locator": "intro and paragraph 3"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_eternal_nightmare", "locator": "lead; Kitava page"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "The Beast"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "The Beast section"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "Summary section"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_faridun", "locator": "Events in Path of Exile 2"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "The Beast dialogue"}]

name: Chaos
aliases: ["Chaos (Impulse)", "Impulse of Chaos", "Lord Chaos", "Master of the Trialmaster"]

summary: Animalistic gods worshipped by the Ezomytes, believed to roam the realm of Spirit; their avatars are Spirit Beasts: Saqawal (birds/reptiles, 'Last of the First'), Farrul (hounds/cats/mammals, 'First of the Hunt'), Fenumus (insects, 'First Explorer'), Craiceann (crabs/squid/sea life, 'First of All'). Also The Greatwolf and the Gull.

summary: Unique monster in Act 2 Fellshrine Ruins representing Sin and Innocence's sister, from before the gods; presumably never ascended.

name: The Molten One
summary: Last surviving Titan from a prehistoric era, worshipped indirectly as the volcano home of the Redblade warband; writes environmental lore found in the Forge of the Titans.

aliases: ["Father of War", "Tukohama, Karui God of War"]
summary: Karui god of war; his tooth slashed Kitava's face. Revived by the Beast's death, he raises the Karui Fortress and is the first god the Exile captures for the Pantheon in Act 6. Kaom claimed to be his son (carvings in Kaom's Stronghold).

summary: One of five Breachlords. Cold Breachlord (female per wiki). Boss residing in Tul's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_uul-netol_unburdened_flesh", "locator": "lead + Version History"}]

summary: Shadowy Vaal spirit entity at the top of the Ancient Pyramid; final boss of Act 2; summoned by The Apex on the Dark Altar.

summary: Karui god of storms and lightning; his jaw became a fish hook, one of Kitava's Torments.

name: Viridi
summary: Third sister of Solaris and Lunaris, Azmeri goddess of the earth, trapped within 'the orb' in Azmeri creation myth; probable namesake of the Viridian Wildwood.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_viridi", "locator": "intro and 'Lore'"}]

PoE1 fought it as Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand; in PoE2 0.5 it is the Breach pinnacle ('Xesht, We That Are One' per a guide), reached through a Breachstone/Realmgate.

summary: One of five Breachlords (fire). Boss of Xoph's Domain, accessed via Xoph's Breachstone in a map device (2.5.0; removed from game 3.28.0). Model based on a Marauder; one of four lords fused into Xesht.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_xoph_dark_embers", "locator": "lead + Version History"}]

name: Yaomac
summary: Ancient Vaal god with three serpentine heads, worshipped by Vaalish priests. Ixchel stole his sleeping body for the Order of the Djinn; the Trialmaster refers to Yaomac when the player wins five or more times.

aliases: ["Ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui Era"]

summary: Umbrella period of the Eternal Empire (Sarn Empire) from Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC) through the Reign of Voll to the Cataclysm (~1339 IC). Split into the era_eternal_empire_rise and era_eternal_empire_fall buckets; the faction itself is faction_eternal_empire.

chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "c. 334 IC to c. 1339 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: The later Eternal Empire: Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth (1317 IC), Chitus and the gemling legions, the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) and the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) that ends the empire. Boundary with the 'rise' bucket is a convention.

name: Eternal Empire Rise
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "1 IC to c. 334 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: From 1 IC: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn and the Eternal Empire; the empire expands; the Night of a Thousand Ribbons (c. 334 IC) ends Romira's reign.

summary: Umbrella for the PoE2-era buckets: the Acts 1-6 campaign and interludes (era_poe2_campaign) and endgame and league storylines (era_poe2_endgame). Begins after the ~20-year interlude following the PoE1 kill of the Beast. Meta grouping only.

summary: The PoE2 campaign: the Exile chases the Seed of Corruption across Wraeclast, starting in Ogham (Act 1).

summary: PoE2 endgame storylines after the campaign. Not covered in detail in this domain.

name: Post-Cataclysm Oriath
summary: Oriath, the island unaffected by the Cataclysm, becomes a Templar theocracy; the Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius. Roughly 260 years pass before PoE1.

chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "before the Vaal; earliest prehistory (exact years unknown)", "story_order": null}

summary: The Vaal Empire under Queen Atziri, the use of virtue gems and sacrifice, ending in the Vaal Cataclysm.

summary: Alano sealed the dark being in 35 IC; darkness lifted.

chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "1334 IC (Night of a Thousand Ribbons)", "story_order": null}
summary: During the Night of a Thousand Ribbons celebration in Sarn, Victario's rebels ambushed the event. Mayor Ondar, who had gems implanted for it, betrayed Emperor Chitus and killed him.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Assassination of Chitus'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'Assassination of Chitus' (ambush, Ondar betrayal; Origins footnotes)"}]

summary: After the Cataclysm Atziri kept her beauty at the cost of her humanity, relegated to a nightmare realm where sacrificed Vaal rise and die repeatedly; her influence later seeps back via Vaal side areas and corruption.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_atziri_lore", "locator": "section 'Post Fall'"}]

summary: In his last moments Aul rapidly crystallises his citadel with azurite, becoming the Crystal King.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_ahn_s_citadel", "locator": "flavour text"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Primeval civilization > Aul: 'In the final moments of his reign, he enacted the final ritual, encasing his palace in crystals'"}]

name: Aul and Kulemak's Bargain
summary: Weakened Kulemak offers Aul 'untold power and mastery' for a single golem; the golem is infused with necromancy and the first Lightless/possessed golems result, ultimately toppling the primeval civilisation.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Primeval civilization: Aul"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lightless", "locator": "Kulemak"}]

summary: Aul, a slave, overthrows the tyrant Putembo and becomes the Crystal King.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Primeval civilization: Aul's Uprising"}]

name: Release Balbala in Traitor's Passage
summary: Using Risu's passage, the Exile climbs Traitor's Passage and defeats Balbala, releasing the sealed Djinn.

summary: Rebel assault led by Victario with Templars, Ezomytes, Maraketh and Karui; repulsed by Chitus' gemlings, Marylene died shielding Victario.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Battle at the Grain Gate'"}]

name: Battle of Lioneye's Watch
summary: Kaom's ambush kills Lioneye.

summary: 1333 IC Ezomyte victory at Glarryn.

summary: Cadiro Perandus negotiates Sarn's unconditional surrender to Voll on 1 Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC after stealing the treasury.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Assassination of Chitus', last paragraph"}]

name: Chitus crowned Emperor
summary: Crowned 1319 IC; seals Izaro in.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Chitus'"}]

name: Keth: the Essence of Water
summary: Following the sand-buried city of Keth, the Exile defeats Azarian, the Forsaken Son, and burns the Water Goddess Halani at her request to recover the Essence of Water.
curation: ["codex audit round 2: relic errands in any order"]
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_city_of_seven_waters", "locator": "Walkthrough 'Defeat Azarian' / 'End the Water Goddess' suffering'"}]

summary: Sin planted the Dark Ember/Seed of Corruption beneath Highgate and nurtured it into the Beast to suppress the gods and end mortal ascension. PoE2 wiki adds that Sin sought Kalandra's cryptic advice and found the Seed in a Precursor ruin.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "'The Beast'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 3"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "section 'The Beast'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 2: Sin ... sought the ancient being Kalandra ... found a Precursor ruin containing the Seed of Corruption"}]

sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_a_crown_of_stone", "locator": "Walkthrough 'Defeat Zalmarath, the Colossus'"}]

summary: c. 1450 IC (History of Wraeclast); contradicts the use of his spirit's Eye of Desire in 1336 IC, which the wiki leaves unexplained.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Daresso and Merveil'"}]

name: Death of Geofri
summary: 1332 IC; Maligaro ambushes templars.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Death of Geofri'"}]

name: Kaom's march on Highgate and death
summary: Lured by the Beast's voice posing as Tukohama, Kaom led 500 warriors to Highgate and was deceived into slaying them before dying; his Eye of Fury was taken.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Lioneye's Watch' subsection, Kaom's march to Highgate"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_king_kaom", "locator": "History"}]

name: Defeat of Titucius
summary: 3rd Galvano of Vitali 1333 IC; Maraketh storm trap.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Defeat of Titucius'"}]

name: Deshret seals the mines
summary: Twenty years after Kaom.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Deshret's Seal'"}]

name: Gemlings fall with Chitus
summary: With Chitus' death his master gem stopped and the legionnaires linked to his heartbeat died; Captain Alsarus' legion survived beyond the perimeter.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Assassination of Chitus'"}]

summary: The Exile fights through Aggorat to the Black Chambers, rescues Alva, and captures Doryani, who agrees to help contain the Beast with a piece of the Precursor weapon.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Capture Doryani for his knowledge of the Beast'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Capture Doryani"}]

summary: In the present Doryani confirms he holds one piece of an ancient anti-Corruption weapon; Alva proposes Kingsmarch as a base, and the Hooded One decides the group should travel south to Ngamakanui to find the other pieces.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Speak to Alva' / 'Travel to Kingsmarch'"}]

summary: The Exile boards the Dreadnought; Jamanra the Abomination fights, the Countess escapes, and Asala beheads Jamanra. The Beast escapes with the Countess once more.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat Jamanra, the Abomination' / 'Speak to Asala'"}]

name: Earn passage on the Ardura caravan
summary: The Exile defeats the Sun Clan hyenas and their leader Rathbreaker for Zarka, who admits the Exile to the Ardura akhara as a jingakh.

summary: c. 1339 IC; Malachai takes control of the Beast; Empire falls.

summary: Ezomyte cataclysm: the First Ones, unhonoured, spill fire out of a mountain; leaders turned to ash, survivors fed on tainted grain from Mother Gull. PoE2 reveals it is the Winter of the World.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ezomytes", "locator": "History > The Great Fire"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Ezomytes > The Great Fire"}]

name: Great Wasting
summary: Karui name for the apocalyptic age of horror and famine also called the Great Fire (Ezomyte) and Winter of the World (Maraketh); Karui ancestors and Maraketh gods are said to emerge in it.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Gods > The Great Wasting"}]

name: First battle at the Halani Gates
summary: The Exile opens the gates with Asala; Jamanra, the Risen King, is fought at the gates and retreats behind an impassable sandstorm (Faridun page), while the Countess escapes.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest 'Open the third Gate' / 'Return to the Ardura Caravan'"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_6W2cqV9l3wE", "locator": "[14:20] Halani Gates closed; [23:10] Countess described (auto-captions)"}]

name: The Hooded One reveals he is Sin
summary: At a shrine northwest of the caravan, the Hooded One confesses he is Sin, the Thief of Virtue, and that he created the Beast; he sends the Exile south into the long-ago Vaal jungles to find a way to drain the Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest log 'Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine to the Northwest' (quote 'I am... a god. I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin.')"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_6W2cqV9l3wE", "locator": "[77:11] 'I am the thief of virtue.' / [77:14] 'I am sin.' (Gavryn, Act 2 full dialogue, auto-captions)"}]

name: Recreate the Horn of the Vastiri
summary: With Zarka, the Exile reforges the Horn of the Vastiri from the three sub-quest items to counter Jamanra's sandstorm, retracing Orbala's footsteps.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest log 'Recreate the Horn of the Vastiri'"}]

name: Imperialis Conceptus
summary: Founding of the Eternal Empire (1 IC).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_tarcus_veruso", "locator": "'Imperialus Conceptus'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)'"}]

name: Innocence's true ascension (Sanctum relic account)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "before Templar order; Azmeri era", "story_order": null}
summary: Lore revealed through Sanctum unique relics: Sin and Innocence were brothers among the Azmeri; Innocence founded a religion on fear of the 'cleansing fire' and the newcomers' symbol, branded Sin the embodiment of sin, and both ascended (Sin ashen, Innocence golden), until the Azmeri drove Innocence's followers off the mountains. Contradicts the Templar 'mother of two' propaganda.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_yt_7QuY96FyhG4", "locator": "[24:37]-[32:00] Lycia's relic text account; [43:03]-[44:30] mother of two as fabrication"}]

name: Kalandra Trapped in the Lake
summary: Kalandra enters the primordial lake out of curiosity and can never leave: every escape returns her to the lake with no memory.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore > Ancient Etchings"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Lake of Kalandra"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore: Ancient Etchings; History of Wraeclast 'The Lake of Kalandra'"}]

name: Kalguuran Expedition to Wraeclast
summary: After the Vaal Cataclysm's omens, King Cadigan III sends an expedition with the Triskelion Flame led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved; they colonise Vaal ruins, until horrors, a priesthood plot and the loss of the Flame destroy the colony.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Kalguur > Expedition to Wraeclast"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "History"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Kalguur' (Expedition to Wraeclast; Shrine)"}]

name: Kaom at Highgate
summary: Kaom slays his 500 warriors deceived by the Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Axiom Prison' end"}]

name: Kitava invited into Wraeclast
summary: Karui carvings say the Eternals opened the gate and invited Kitava into the land; Kitava cut the Karui off from the Ancestors. Haku adds that the Karui also had a hand in the downfall.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_ingame_haku_navali_dialogue", "locator": "Weathered Carving in Kaom's Stronghold; Haku 'The Karui and Wraeclast'"}]

name: Lightless Invasion
summary: After ash blocked the sun, the Lightless surface and devastate the primeval civilisation, felled Titans and the Maraketh/Azmeri cultures; a coalition under the Third Pact opposes them.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro; The Winter of the World"}]

name: Opening of the Lord's Labyrinth
summary: Izaro opens the maze on 1317 IC; Chitus and Weylin enter; Chitus poisons Weylin.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'The Lord's Labyrinth'"}]

name: Lord's Labyrinth Opened
summary: Izaro opens the Lord's Labyrinth on the second Galvano of Azmeri, 1317 IC. Chitus wins it by betraying Weylin, and then seals Izaro inside.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' and 'Reign of Chitus'"}]

name: Lycia's pact with Beidat
summary: Lycia, shocked by the unnamed discarded bones of the Templar ossuary and the true origin of Innocence, called Beidat and traded her freedom for immortality inside the Sanctum, giving the Scourge a foothold in Wraeclast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_yt_7QuY96FyhG4", "locator": "[9:39]-[11:30], [35:07]-[35:36]"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_lycia_herald_of_the_scourge", "locator": "page summary"}]

name: Slay Count Geonor in Ogham Manor
summary: The Exile infiltrates Ogham Manor and kills Count Geonor, freeing Ogham; Oriana escapes with the Beast, and the Hooded One sends the Exile east toward the Vastiri.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_mad_wolf_of_ogham", "locator": "Quest 'Kill the Mad Wolf' / 'Return to Town'"}]

name: Malachai spared by Voll
summary: Malachai promises end of thaumaturgy.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Voll'"}]

name: Maraketh Golden Age
summary: Roughly a thousand years of glory after Solerai and Lundara expelled the Lightless, in a lush Vastiri of seven rivers; ended when the Beast silenced the gods.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Maraketh paragraph 2"}]

name: Drain the lake through the Matlan Waterways
summary: The Exile powers the Infested Barrens altar with the large Soul Core and activates the Matlan Waterways, revealing the Sunken City of Utzaal.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Activate The Matlan Waterways' / 'Talk to Alva'"}]

name: Rudja and the Faridun defector at Mawdun Mine
summary: At Mawdun Quarry and Mine, the Exile defeats Rudja and frees the defector Risu, who reveals Jamanra's plan to feed the Beast and that the Halani Gates are closed.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat Rudja, Dread Engineer' / 'Talk to Risu about the closed Gates'"}]

name: Medved's challenge
summary: A two-axe horror leader (recognised by Vorana as her beloved Medved) killed 42 challengers in 42 days; Vorana ordered a retreat; two villages fell.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Medved's challenge'"}]

name: Night of a Thousand Ribbons
summary: Burning of Sarn in protest against Romira; later festival where Chitus was assassinated.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "same"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'"}]

name: Order of the Djinn Forsake Kalandra
summary: The Order of the Djinn swears to free Kalandra and devotes itself to her artefacts of power, but 'once they understood the truth of this place' its scribes try to erase her from history, burning their books (Kalandra page: and self-immolating out of fear); the History page words it as forsaking and abandoning her.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Ancient Etching VI summary"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Lake of Kalandra"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore > Ancient Etchings: 'burning their books and self-immolating out of fear'"}]

name: Oriath destroyed by Sirus
summary: PoE1 Conquerors of the Atlas: Oriath is completely destroyed by Sirus, leaving it devastated; PoE2 states the world believed Oriath abandoned twenty years ago after crises.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Sirus section"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "Conquerors of the Atlas paragraph"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_5", "locator": "intro"}]

name: Original Sin (Innocence's ascension)
summary: Per Lycia's relics, twin brothers Innocence and Sin lived among the Azmeri; Innocence, unable to attract enough followers, turned his followers against Sin and used their hatred to ascend, leaving Sin blackened. The Templar stained-glass version is propaganda.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "'Original Sin'"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_7QuY96FyhG4", "locator": "[24:08]"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "section on Forbidden Sanctum relics / Lycia's findings; 'Original Sin' unique"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_7QuY96FyhG4", "locator": "[24:43]-[25:12] Lycia's story of Sin and Innocence among the Azmeri"}]

name: Perpetual Night over the Imperial Heartlands
chronology: {"in_world_year": 35, "relative": "Caspiro died ~5 years after Veruso; Alano Phrecia quote dated first Sacrato of Lurici, 35 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: Azmerian writers describe part of the empire cast into perpetual night, a 'dark being' dismembering Emperor Caspiro, until General Alano Phrecia dispelled it, 'returning the gaze of Solaris'. Likely the darkness later sealed in the Oversoul (per GGG Q&A).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "Reign of Caspiro / Alano Phrecia"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Reign of Caspiro; Alano Phrecia"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "Alano Phrecia quote: '... our legions drove the dark being deep into the recesses of its lair and sealed it away for eternity' (35 IC)"}]

name: Plague of Ezomyr
summary: At some point most of Ezomyr was wiped out by a plague (per Kahuturoa), after Oriath was recently established.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Ezomytes; The Caaltu"}]

name: The Trials of Chaos (PoE2 Act 3 quest)
summary: Optional Act 3 quest: after obtaining an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian), the Exile places it in the Temple of Chaos offering and completes the Trialmaster's Challenges for 2 Ascendancy Points. The PoE2 entry point to the Trial of Chaos ascension trial.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trials_of_chaos", "locator": "Infobox (act 3, optional, start 'Acquire an Inscribed Ultimatum', boss Xyclucian, the Chimera); '===Place the Inscribed Ultimatum in the Temple Offering===' and '===Quest Complete=== (2 Ascendancy Points)'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trial_of_chaos", "locator": "Access section (Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian; Temple of Chaos offering); lead ('based on Ultimatum from PoE1')"}]

name: Exile travels to Utzaal's past
summary: The Exile and Alva use the gateway to reach Utzaal before the Cataclysm to learn of the Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Enter the Time Portal"}]

name: Arrival in Kingsmarch
summary: Exile, Hooded One and Doryani reach Kingsmarch to find the Weapon; Doryani laments science never recovered; the Hooded One says the Kalguurans 'have potential'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Talk to Doryani"}]

name: Alliance plan against Oriath
summary: The Hooded One decides to call the Ezomytes, Maraketh and Vaal (Doryani's reserves) to war before assaulting Oriath; the Karui are already allied.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Speak to the Hooded One"}]

name: Exile defeats Benedictus
summary: In the Excavation the Countess leaves Benedictus to hold the Exile; he is defeated, and Kanu, begging to be taken along, reveals the Beast is in Oriath before Tavakai strikes him down.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Confront Kanu and the First Herald; Defeat Benedictus"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Defeat Benedictus"}]

name: Tavakai defeated at Heart of the Tribe
summary: Tavakai fights in three phases; Tukohama rejects him ('This... is not the Way'); the Exile defeats him.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Defeat Tavakai"}]

name: Exile defeats Torvian
summary: On Arastas the Exile defeats Torvian, Hand of the Saviour, after the Twilight Order ambush at the church.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Defeat Torvian, Hand of the Saviour"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "Progression: Arastas boss"}]

name: Freeing the Trickster at Journey's End
summary: Exile frees 'Freya Hartlin' with Verisium Spikes; she reveals herself as Tangmazu, triggering a Delirium encounter with Omniphobia.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_dark_mists", "locator": "final paragraph"}]

name: Charter of the Aurora May
summary: Alva introduces Rog, who sells a Boat Charter for Vaal treasure; Makoru and Kanu will take the Exile to the most dangerous islands.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Talk to Alva; Take the Boat Charter"}]

name: Island search for weapon pieces
summary: The Exile sails the Karui islands (e.g. Isle of Kin, Shrike Island, Whakapanu, Abandoned Prison) to find the three Weapon pieces, whose island locations rotate; bosses include Krutog, Diamora, the Prisoner and the Scourge of the Skies. Kedge Bay is separate Dark Mists content.
curation: ["codex audit round 2: Kedge Bay holds no Weapon piece"]
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "Progression + piece table"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Explore the Islands"}]

name: Hooded One recalls Precursor script
summary: On the first and second Weapon pieces the Hooded One recognises Precursor writing from a faded mortal memory (a woman's lap, a vivid book; later: sent to live among the Azmeri with a brother and sister, but earlier 'somewhere else' with works of stone, metal and glass).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Witness the Hooded One (1st and 2nd pieces)"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Witness The Hooded One (first and second pieces)"}]

name: Weapon reforged; Third Edict revealed
aliases: ["The Weapon is reforged; Third Edict revealed"]
summary: In the Excavated Site the Hooded One reforges the Weapon and Tavakai seizes it; back in Kingsmarch the Hooded One reads the inscription 'The instrument of the Third Edict', made to cleanse Corruption and destroy the Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon; Return to Kingsmarch"}]

name: Sin cures Tavakai and Makoru
summary: The Hooded One, called Sin in the quest log, cures Tavakai and Makoru of Blood Fever with the Weapon; Tavakai pledges the Karui to fight Oriana.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Witness Sin cure Tavakai and Makoru"}]

name: Tavakai seizes the Weapon
summary: After the reforging Tavakai takes the Weapon for the Karui and flees to Ngakanu with Makoru; the Hooded One warns of its Corruption.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon"}]

name: Utopia on Arastas
summary: Missionary Lorandis sends the Exile to Arastas to swear an oath to the Saviour; Servitor Marius offers Utopia; refusal completes the quest, and Benedictus and Kanu's treachery follow.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_utopia", "locator": "Quest description"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Travel to Arastas"}]

name: Ancient Gateway and the Fortress Gateways
summary: After the Fortress rises, the Exile travels to the Ancient Gateway, uses levers to reach the central platform, summons Doryani and activates another Precursor Beacon, which opens the way to the Burning Monolith (quest log, Legacy of the Precursors).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest log: 'Travel to the Ancient Gateway', 'Defeat the Precursor Separator', 'Ride the Elevator'"}]

name: Gods awaken after the Beast's death
summary: About 20 years before PoE2 an exile killed the Beast, waking the slumbering gods, who per the Twilight Order now make civilisation impossible.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 4"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_twilight_order", "locator": "art book quote"}]

name: Waking the Dreamer
summary: 0.5 Breach story: travel to the Monastery of the Keepers and the Genesis Tree; defeat It That Was Tul and It That Was Esh (Sky Fortress bosses; official notes: they yield the key to the Breach pinnacle) and retrieve the Breachlord Sac to reach the Dreamer; later fight Xesht. Hiveborn details come from press coverage.

summary: Endgame site reached during Legacy of the Precursors ('Reach the Burning Monolith') after the Ancient Gateway. In 0.1-0.4 it was found directly on the Atlas and opened with three Crisis Fragments (The Pinnacle of Flame); in 0.5 it stands inside the Precursor Fortress.

name: Clearing the Way (PoE2 quest)
summary: Optional Interlude 2 quest: Risu asks the Exile to slay the scorpion Akthi, the Final Sting, and the sandworm Anundr at the far end of the Khari Crossing so the other akharas can join the Gifting of Water. The reward is a Book of Specialisation.

summary: Required epilogue endgame quest tied to Hilda: automatically started near Hilda's Campsite, the Exile finds Hilda and defeats four Great Beasts in turn, speaking with her between fights; the quest completes after the fourth. The wiki page is a stub; quest steps are listed without rewards.

name: Hostile Takeover (PoE2 quest)

sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_hostile_takeover", "locator": "intro"}]

name: Recruit the Ezomytes (Curse of Holten)
summary: Exile kills Isolde, Heldra, Siora, then Thane Wulfric and Lady Elswyth, ending Holten's blight; Renly pledges all clans to the war.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_recruit_the_ezomytes", "locator": "Quest log"}]

name: Recruit the Maraketh (The Stolen Barya)
summary: Exile defeats Elzarah, Vornas and Prince Azmadi to save the First Barya; Asala completes the Gifting of Water and brings the Maraketh to Kingsmarch.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_recruit_the_maraketh", "locator": "Quest log"}]

name: Recruit the Vaal (Doryani's Contingency)
summary: The code phrase 'the time of the sparrow has come' and defeat of Rakkar, Stormgore, Zolin and Zelina secures the Cuachic.

name: Landing at the Ziggurat Refuge
summary: Siege of Oriath ends not at Oriath but at the Ziggurat Refuge; Quest Complete text says 'despite your attempts to travel to Oriath'. Why is not stated; the Beast's corruption holds the Hooded One in thrall afterwards.

name: Vessel of Kulemak
summary: Pinnacle Abyss encounter, the Vessel of Kulemak: Kulemak's Invitation (dropped by Abyssal commanders per guides) sends the player into the Well and the Black Cathedral. Guides say defeating it unlocks the Abyssal Lich ascendancy (exact conditions vary by guide/patch); fully empowering it means defeating the Lich Lords Kurgal, Ulaman and Amanamu.

name: Land of the Kin (PoE2 quest)
summary: Required Act 4 side quest, begun by speaking to Makoru and sailing to the Isle of Kin; the Exile explores the Isle and Volcanic Warrens to kill Krutog, Lord of Kin. Part of the rotating Act 4 requirements.

name: Legacy of the Maji (endgame quest)
summary: Endgame quest begun by finding Aoife near a Ritual Altar: she was killed by the King in the Mists (the King of the Nameless); the Exile destroys his effigies, kills him again at the Crux of Nothingness, takes his Head and Aoife's body, performs the Rite of the Nameless over five maps and defeats the Bodach. Quest complete: 'You have defeated The Bodach and Aoife is finally at peace.' (steps from a hidden comment block).

name: The Origin Core and the Origin Tower
summary: Combining the Origin Cradle and Origin Spark (from the Matriarch and Patriarch Halls) in the Precursor Reactor yields the Origin Core; when the Exile places it in the Origin Tower, Tecrod's wyrm incapacitates the Exile and Tecrod exults 'With this, the Master shall know unending power!' before the Arbiter of Divinity destroys his body.

name: The Pinnacle of Flame (removed quest)
summary: Epilogue/endgame quest of 0.1-0.4: find the Burning Monolith on the endgame map and collect three Crisis Fragments to open the door to the Arbiter of Ash. Removed in 0.5.0 and folded into Legacy of the Precursors.

Source steps sit in a hidden comment block of the quest log (medium).
