name: Whakapanu Island (PoE2 quest)
summary: Required Act 4 side quest, begun by speaking to Makoru and sailing to Whakapanu Island; the Exile enters the Singing Caverns and kills the Siren Diamora. Part of the rotating Act 4 requirements.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_whakapanu_island_quest", "locator": "Infobox (required: Yes, act 4, start 'Sailing to Whakapanu Island', completion 'Defeat Diamora, Song of Death'); quest log '===Enter the Singing Caverns===' to '===Kill Diamora==='"}]

name: Precursor Cataclysm
summary: After mastering corruption the Precursors delved into world secrets, triggering great fires, eruptions and impacts from the sky; the civilisation was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm. Cause unclear.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro; Precursor civilization"}]

name: Priesthood conspiracy (stabbing of Olroth)
summary: High Priest Uhtred, suspecting Olroth of fighting for the horrors in his sleep, had a dozen priests stab him (71 wounds); Vorana killed all twelve; Olroth was encased in glass and Uhtred fled to an ancient site of power.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Priesthood conspiracy'; 'The Shrine'"}]

name: Purity Rebellion
summary: A rebellion led by High Templar Voll and the poet Victario, with King Kaom, Sekhema Deshret and Thane Rigwald. It culminates in the siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC) and Voll's coronation.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "sections 'The Purity Rebellion', 'Siege of Sarn', 'Assassination of Chitus'"}, {"source_id": "src_book_path_of_exile_origins", "locator": "issues #1-4 (Death to Sin / The Black Heart)"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_voll_emperor_of_purity", "locator": "Lore"}]

name: The Temple Door Idol from the Queen of Filth
summary: The Exile enters the Drowned City and Aggorat, defeats the Queen of Filth, and takes the Temple Door Idol to open the Temple of Kopec.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat the Queen of Filth' / 'Pick up the Temple Door Idol'"}]

name: Rapture Device activation
summary: 1336 IC; Dialla refuses; Malachai enters Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Voll'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_rapture_device", "locator": "lead"}]

name: Slay the Bloated Miller
summary: The Exile follows a wounded man's warning to Clearfell, kills the Bloated Miller, and receives a reward from Renly (the quest is on The Riverbank; the Miller attacks the camp).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_reaching_clearfell", "locator": "Walkthrough"}]

name: The Red Communion
summary: Project that allowed Atziri to commune directly with the Beast. Doryani, privately opposed, was forced to devise it; he learned all he could and prepared contingencies. It triggered the Vaal Cataclysm.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' (PoE2 account)"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Spymaster note: 'consequences of the Red Communion'"}]

name: Return of the Sun
summary: The Winter of the World ends: Maraketh tradition credits twin sekhema Solerai and Lundara expelling the Lightless; official Abyss text credits Solaris. Sources differ (possibly the same figures).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Lightless final paragraph; The Maraketh"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_maraketh", "locator": "Solerai and Lundara"}]

name: Dispel the sandstorm with the Horn of the Vastiri
summary: The Exile sounds the Horn of the Vastiri at the sandstorm, dispelling Jamanra's barrier, and Asala then turns the caravan toward Deshar.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest 'Use the Horn of the Vastiri' / 'Speak to Asala'"}]

name: Release the Hooded One from the Tree of Souls
summary: In the Grelwood the Exile finds the Tree of Souls holding the Hooded One; Una says only runes can break the binding, so the Exile collects Runes of Power from the Red Vale and stabs them into the Tree with the forged Rune Spikes.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_secrets_in_the_dark", "locator": "Quest 'Use the Rune Spikes' / 'Speak to Una'"}]

name: Seed of Corruption Released
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "about 20 years after Kitava's defeat", "story_order": null}
summary: About 20 years after Kitava's defeat, Count Geonor pierces the Hooded One with a runic sword and extracts the Seed of Corruption, which begins feeding on a soldier. Corruption spreads across Wraeclast and the Atlas.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_lore", "locator": "section 'Prelude / Count Geonor'"}]

name: Siege of Sarn
summary: On the last day of Divini 1334 IC, High Templar Voll laid siege to Sarn with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh rebel support. Cadiro Perandus negotiated Sarn's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC, and Voll was crowned a week later.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Siege of Sarn'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'Siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC)' and the paragraph after 'Assassination of Chitus' (surrender and coronation)"}]

name: Sin Consults Kalandra
summary: Sin seeks Kalandra at her lake and receives cryptic instructions leading him to a Precursor ruin holding the Seed of Corruption, used to create the Beast. Etching V's 'little thief' is read as Sin; PoE1 link is inference, PoE2 wiki states it directly.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 2"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore, Ancient Etching V"}]

name: Slumber of the Gods
summary: Sin plants the Dark Ember in Highgate, creating the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy. The Beast initiates the Slumber of the Gods, which puts all gods to sleep.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro paragraph 3"}]

name: Slumbering of the Gods
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "unknown, millennia before PoE1 (before the Vaal Empire per PoE2 wiki)", "story_order": null}
summary: Sin's Beast lulled the gods into dreamless slumber, ending an era of divine strife; Hinekora foresaw it and prepared the Halls of the Dead before sleeping.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_ingame_sin_dialogue", "locator": "Sin 'The Rise of the Gods': \"We gods, we were driven into slumbering darkness, to dream away eternity whilst the gentle Beast watched over us.\""}, {"source_id": "src_ingame_hinekora_dialogue", "locator": "Hinekora dream: 'She foresaw the Slumbering of the Gods' / hinekora wiki Lore"}]

name: Open the Memorial Gate for Lachlann
summary: In the Cemetery of the Eternals the Exile destroys Asinia and Praetor Draven for the two Memorial Key pieces, opens the gate, and puts Lachlann to rest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_sorrow_among_stones", "locator": "Quest 'Follow Lachlann' / 'End Lachlann's Suffering'"}]

name: Templars shift to Oriath
summary: After the Cataclysm.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "'Lore'"}]

name: Templar Theocracy of Oriath
summary: After the Cataclysm, the Templars shift their base to Oriath and develop a theocracy. The Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius shortly before PoE1.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "section 'Lore' (Templars shift base to Oriath)"}]

name: Defeat Ketzuli in the Temple of Kopec
summary: In the Temple of Kopec the Exile defeats Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun, and Alva activates an elevator and gateway into the Ziggurat's past.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun' / 'Ride the Elevator'"}]

name: Revive the Hooded One with Count Lachlann's ring
summary: Through the Grim Tangle, the Exile brings Count Lachlann's ring to Una, who revives the Hooded One; he reveals the Seed of Corruption is in Ogham and must be recovered.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_mysterious_shade", "locator": "Quest 'Witness the revival of the Hooded One'"}]

name: Mastodon Tusks from the Bone Pits
summary: In the Bone Pits the Exile defeats Ekbab and Iktab for the Mastodon Tusks that Jamanra wanted for lightning powers.
curation: ["codex audit round 2: relic errands in any order"]
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_a_theft_of_ivory", "locator": "Walkthrough 'Defeat Ekbab, Ancient Steed and Iktab'"}]

name: Enter the time gateway to Utzaal's past
summary: The gateway sends the Exile and Alva into Utzaal's past, where the Vaal see Alva and the Exile as threats while the Cataclysm is imminent.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Enter the Time Portal' / 'Enter Utzaal in the past'"}]

name: Titans and Humans Fight the Rising Darkness
summary: A 'rising darkness' (likely the Lightless after the Winter of the World) attacks Titans and humans; surviving Titans forge weapons and unearth the first virtue gem, but are almost wiped out.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > The Titans"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_molten_one", "locator": "The Alliance Against Darkness"}]

name: Defeat Tor Gul in the Spires of Deshar
summary: In Deshar the Exile climbs the Path of Mourning to the Spires, where the Faridun have taken the honoured dead, and defeats Tor Gul, the Defiler.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat Tor Gul, the Defiler'"}]

name: Kill the Executioner and free Leitis
summary: The Exile finds the Executioner at Ogham Village, frees his prisoner Leitis, and Leitis (who says 'He killed Eamon') then asks the Exile to depose Count Geonor.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption", "locator": "Quest 'Talk to Leitis' / 'Quest Complete'"}]

name: Merchant Wars and War of the Great Families
summary: Feud between House Keita and House Bardiya that escalated into civil war and ended in a ceasefire and the Merchant Council.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_trarthus", "locator": "History"}]

name: Trarthan Rebellion against Phrecius (870 IC)
summary: Warlords of Trarthus were executed after Phrecian legions occupied it; four first-generation Trarthans led a war; Karui blockades and Ezomyte sabotage doomed reinforcements; Tyndarus capitulated after two years.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_trarthus", "locator": "History"}]

name: Trarthan War of Independence
summary: 870-872 IC rebellion against Tyndarus.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_trarthus", "locator": "'History'"}]

name: Trial of the Ancestors
summary: Tournament in the Halls of the Dead where the Exile's team of Karui warriors fights teams led by the ten Karui chieftains, destroying totems; winning a full tournament earns rewards from Hinekora (omens, Hinekora's Lock, unique items).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_ancestor_league", "locator": "'==League mechanic=='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_hinekora", "locator": "'rules over the Halls of the Dead and oversees the Trial of the Ancestors'"}]

name: Trials of Chaos
summary: Escalating wave trials in which a Trialmaster-set modifier is added each round; the player banks or risks rewards. PoE1 Ultimatum league (3.14), core in 3.23; PoE2 Ascension Trial of Chaos (Act 3 Temple of Chaos, up to 10 trials).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_ultimatum_league", "locator": "lead; League mechanic"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trial_of_chaos", "locator": "lead and Access"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trials_of_chaos", "locator": "Walkthrough"}]

name: Loss of the Triskelion Flame
summary: The starlight barrier vanished as Vorana tried to adjust it; the Flame's altar was empty and all harbour ships but one had been burned. Vorana branded Uhtred a traitor, and Olroth's glass case was found empty. Uhtred had fled to an ancient shrine.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Medved's challenge' end; 'Aftermath' note"}]

name: Twilight Order rebuilds Oriath
summary: After the abandonment, the Twilight Order emerged from secrecy and rebuilt Oriath in secret; Act 5 is set there and the Beast is held there (per Kanu).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_twilight_order", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_5", "locator": "intro: 'Oriath, which was rebuilt in secret'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Kanu: 'they're in Oriath'"}]

name: Survive the Utzaal Cataclysm through the gateway
summary: The Exile and Alva survive the Cataclysm in Utzaal's past and return through the gateway with Doryani, who then laments that his people are long dead.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Use the Gateway' / 'Survive the Cataclysm'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Survive the Cataclysm"}]

name: Vaal first contact with the Azmeri
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "c. 1160 BC (~2,500 years before Chitus, per Trinian)", "story_order": null}
summary: Around 1160 BC (Trinian, writing c. 1333 IC, says about 2,500 years earlier) the Vaal first contacted the primitive Azmeri tribes of the Azmerian ranges, introducing agriculture and literacy and helping create the first Azmerian written language, while never divulging the secret of virtue gems.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'Contacting the Azmeri'; Trinian, The Ancients Book 4"}]

name: Vaal Cataclysm
summary: Event c. 400 BIC that ended the Vaal Empire: Doryani's project to grant immortality (manipulating the Beast, corruption, gems, sacrifice and 'communion') went wrong; only 3,126 Vaal survived and took refuge with the Azmeri. PoE2 shows the Red Communion and Atziri being swallowed by the Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Vaal Cataclysm'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' (paragraph on Path of Exile 2: Fate of the Vaal)"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'The Vaal Cataclysm'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_doryani", "locator": "section 'Vaal Cataclysm'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_atziri_the_red_queen", "locator": "Abilities: 'cutscene... swallowed by the Beast and starting the Cataclysm'"}]

name: Survivors among the Azmeri
summary: The 3,126 surviving Vaal found refuge among the Azmeri, could not explain what happened, had no gems and assimilated until none remained; they panicked at an image of a gem shown by the Kalguur.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "The Vaal Cataclysm; Dannig, 'Arrival III'"}]

name: Vastiri Becomes a Desert
summary: Over thousands of years the plains' rivers dried and forests became sand, naturally or via Maraketh/Halani-linked causes; the Maraketh became semi-nomadic.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Maraketh paragraph 3; Halani"}]

name: Defeat Viper Napuatzi in Utzaal's past
summary: In Utzaal's past the Vaal general Viper Napuatzi has Alva taken to Doryani; the Exile defeats Napuatzi to open the path.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat Viper Napuatzi' / 'Rescue Alva'"}]

name: Ban on collecting virtue gems in Kalguur
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "during the reign of Cadigan III (ancient Kalguur)", "story_order": null}
summary: After the Azmeri reacted fearfully to virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third officially banned their collection; the gems never returned to Kalguur (Kalguur page, Thaumaturgy section).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "===Thaumaturgy===: \"after witnessing the Azmeris' fearful reaction towards virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third had officially banned their collection\""}]

name: Voll crowned Emperor
summary: Voll of Thebrus crowned Emperor in Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC (Eternal Empire page: a week after Cadiro's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci; Purity Chronicles Book 1 says the 2nd Sacrato of Phreci).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Assassination of Chitus' end"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_purity_chronicles", "locator": "Book 1"}]

name: Voll's pact with Deshret
summary: Voll promises Sekhema Deshret the return of the Vastiri Plains for Maraketh support; she demands Titucius' skin for a saddle.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Defeat of Titucius'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_purity_chronicles", "locator": "Book 4: The Red Sekhema's Saddle"}]

name: Voll's pact with Kaom
summary: Voll and Victario visit Kaom in Ngamakanui; Voll promises Karui sovereignty over Wraeclast's south shore and freedom for slaves in exchange for attacking Lioneye's Watch.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Lioneye's Watch' subsection"}, {"source_id": "src_book_poe_origins", "locator": "The Karui Way pg. 9"}]

name: Winter of the World
aliases: ["Winter of the World (Great Fire / Great Wasting)"]
summary: Ancient war in which Kulemak and the Lightless blanketed the Vastiri Plains and the surface, ended when the Three Sisters (Solerai/Lundara etc.) destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro paragraph 2"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_three_sisters", "locator": "paragraph 2"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_kulemak", "locator": "paragraph 1: 'Winter of the World ... lasted for centuries'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lightless", "locator": "Winter of the World"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_three_sisters", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ezomytes", "locator": "The Great Fire"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Great Fire: 'revealed that the Great Fire was indeed the same event as the Winter of the World'"}]

name: Defeat Xyclucian and enter the Machinarium
summary: In the Chimeral Wetlands the Exile defeats Xyclucian, the Chimera, and enters Jiquani's Machinarium, where Alva sends them after a small Soul Core.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat Xyclucian, the Chimera' / 'Enter Jiquani's Machinarium'"}]

name: Doryani's investigation of Zerphi
summary: Atziri ordered Doryani to research Zerphi's rejuvenation 'within the realms of possibility... without fear of question or consequence'; Vaal aged 16-26 were sent to him and none survived, the experiments failing.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'Zerphi'; Trinian Book 3"}]

name: Defeat Zicoatl and take the large Soul Core
summary: Inside Jiquani's Sanctum the Exile powers two generators with medium Soul Cores and defeats Zicoatl, Warden of the Core, to take the large Soul Core.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Activate two Generators' / 'Defeat Zicoatl, Warden of the Core'"}]

name: Arrive at the Ziggurat Encampment in Utzaal
summary: The Hooded One sends the Exile to Utzaal; the Exile crosses the Sandswept Marsh to the Ziggurat, meeting Oswald and Alva.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest 'Explore Ziggurat Encampment'"}]

name: The Afarud
summary: Rogue Faridun sect that torments djinn; led by figures such as Ridan, Afarud Commander.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_maraketh", "locator": "Lore > The Afarud"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_mirage_league", "locator": "League content"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_ridan_afarud_commander", "locator": "intro"}]

name: Ardura Akhara
summary: Maraketh akhara (caravan order) led by Sekhema Asala and Zarka that the Exile joins in Act 2.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_earning_passage", "locator": "Walkthrough 'Enter the Ardura Caravan'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest log 'Speak to the Sekhema'"}]

name: Azmeri
summary: Ancient tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who worship Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi and others. Eighty thousand of them under Tarcus Veruso descended into the former Vaal lands and founded the Eternal Empire in 1 IC; the Azmeri of the Forest Encampment and the Wildwood descend from those who stayed behind.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_azmeri", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Azmeri"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_azmeri", "locator": "lead paragraph, 'Notable members'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "section 'The Azmeri' / 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_intruders_in_black", "locator": "Helena dialogue"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "Contacting the Azmeri"}]

name: Black Scythe
summary: Kalguuran mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana, responsible for the expedition's defence and offence. Their artifacts are the currency of the Expedition NPC Tujen.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "'===Society==='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "Culture; Society section"}]

name: Black Scythes
summary: Kalguuran mercenaries led by Vorana, fighting horrors from walls with crossbows.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Colonisation"}]

name: The Caaltu
summary: A civilisation that existed in Kahuturoa's time (Vastiri still forest, Vaal extant, Oriath recently founded, Ezomyr not yet struck by plague) and was only a memory by Maata's time. Little else is known.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Caaltu"}]

name: The Cuachic
summary: Isolated Vaal remnant in Mount Kriar's vault, living under strict control for generations; recruited by Doryani's phrase in PoE2 Interlude.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_recruit_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest complete: Hooded One warning"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_recruit_the_vaal", "locator": "quest log"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Cuachic Legacy"}]

name: Druids of Skothe
summary: Ancient order that venerated the Azmeri Draiocht and practised the mystic arts of the Maji; the Druid (an Ezomyte) was once a member. Wiped out by the King in the Mists and his cultists, who deceived them by disguising himself as a Maji of the old.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_druid", "locator": "page 'Lore': 'The Druid is an Ezomyte who was once part of the Druids of Skothe, an ancient order that venerated the Azmeri Draíocht and practiced the mystic arts of the Maji.'"}]

name: Druids of the Broken Circle
summary: Kalguuran nature-mystics under Medved, named after Olroth's gem use clouded their scrying.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Broken Circle"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "'===Society==='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "Culture; Society section"}]

name: Eternal Empire
chronology: {"in_world_year": 1, "relative": "1 IC to c. 1339 IC; roughly 260 years before PoE1 (1599-1600 IC)", "story_order": null}
summary: Oriathan/imperial civilisation, also called the Sarn Empire, founded in 1 IC by Azmeri migrants under Tarcus Veruso on the ruins of the Vaal capital. Ruled by Emperors from Sarn, it held most of central Wraeclast with a Roman-style legion system until the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) destroyed it; Oriath survived as its successor.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "lead paragraph and sections 'History' through 'The Cataclysm'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_1", "locator": "Act 1: Cemetery of the Eternals / Eternal prison areas"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Eternal Empire'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "lead"}]

name: Ezomytes
summary: Clan people of Ezomyr, subjugated and enslaved by the Eternal Empire. Thane Rigwald rallied them in the Bloody Flowers Rebellion of 1333 IC and they joined the siege of Sarn.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ezomytes", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Ezomytes"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ezomytes", "locator": "lead paragraph, 'Rigwald'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "section 'Bloody Flowers Rebellion'"}]

name: Faridun
summary: Maraketh rejects (flawed or mutated newborns left in the dunes) raised by wandering Faridun tribes in the Vastiri, who accept necromancy and long for reunification with the akharas. In PoE2 Act 2 the Countess recruits them with the promise of resurrecting Jamanra.

name: Gemling Legion
summary: Elite legions of the Eternal Empire created by Malachai: legionnaires infused with virtue gems, led by Captains, which gave the Empire military dominance. Chitus carried a master gem whose heartbeat bound every gemling to his own, so they fell when he died; survivors were transformed by the Cataclysm into the Undying.

name: The Godless Three
summary: Three thaumaturgists trained by Malachai: Shavronne of Umbra, Maligaro the Inquisitor and Doedre Darktongue. Maligaro and Doedre were burned by Voll; Malachai later revived all three to guard his heart, lungs and entrails.

summary: Trarthan Great House. Contract-assassin monopoly.

summary: Trarthan Great House. Financiers; Merchant Council with greatest control today.

name: House Cyaxan
summary: Trarthan Great House. Drug trade, criminal syndicate and mass virtue gem implantation.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_trarthus", "locator": "'===The Great Houses==='"}]

name: House Keita
summary: Trarthan Great House. Slave armies, flesh pits; failed to become a god; founded Korathin 872 IC.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_trarthus", "locator": "'===The Great Houses==='"}]

summary: Runesmith people of Middengard who built Kingsmarch (Rog, Tujen, Dannig, Gwennen), led by the Cadigan kings; PoE1 Settlers of Kalguur continues into PoE2 Act 4.

summary: Seafaring warrior people of the southern archipelago. Under King Kaom they allied with Voll's Purity Rebellion, took Lioneye's Watch and founded the first Karui settlement on the mainland; Kaom later fell at Highgate. The Empire had enslaved Karui under Chitus.

name: Keepers of the Flame (Order of the Purple Flame)
summary: Monastic order founded by Ailith after her visions of the Dreamer; they train in the Monastery to defend Wraeclast against the Hiveborn and tend the Genesis Tree. The PoE2 wiki calls it the Order of the Purple Flame; the Monk class belongs to it. It is a taboo among them to speak the Dreamer's true name (Chayula).

summary: Warriors and military enforcers under direct orders of the King, led by Olroth.

name: The Lightless
summary: Necromantic army of possessed golems created by Kulemak, led by Abyssal Liches; ended the primeval civilisation.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lightless", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_aul_the_crystal_king", "locator": "Lore"}]

name: The Maji
summary: Azmeri vanguard chosen when the Wildwood was made; they purge the Nameless and fight the King in the Mists, forbidden from touching virtue gems ('Tears of the Maji').
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_azmeri", "locator": "Culture > The Maji"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "line 149"}]

name: Maraketh
summary: Desert people of the Vastiri led by Sekhemas, living in akhara (tribes). In 1333 IC Sekhema Deshret joined the Purity Rebellion in exchange for the return of the Vastiri Plains; later, Deshret sealed the Highgate mines. A large tribe lives at Highgate in PoE1; the Ardura akhara and Sekhema Asala appear in PoE2.

name: Meridian Free Traders
summary: Trade guild that sent Raulf to assist executing the Kingsmarch charter; in PoE2 it controls boat charters (Makoru captains the Aurora May under it).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_exploring_kingsmarch", "locator": "Raulf quote"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Makoru quote"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Makoru dialogue"}]

name: House Perandus (Necropolis dead)
summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Perandus Pact'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_necropolis_league", "locator": "'==Items==' Unique items by grave crafting"}]

name: House Phrecia (Necropolis dead)
summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Hand of Phrecia'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_necropolis_league", "locator": "'==Items==' Unique items by grave crafting"}]

name: Priests of the Chalice
summary: Religious order that read the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Expedition; The Shrine"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "'===Society==='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "Society section"}]

name: Order of the Djinn
summary: Secret society founded in ancient times by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper (Ahkeli) that protects Wraeclast from calamity and guards dangerous artefacts (Forbidden Vaults near the Oasis, Act 9); takes one orphan from each culture. Members forged and delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay (video). Janus Perandus's betrayal let Catarina raid the vault and the Order was slain except Jun and Janus; in PoE2 Jun is rebuilding it. Past members include Ixchel (later the Trialmaster).

name: Perandus family
summary: Wealthiest merchant-lender family of the Eternal Empire (motto 'With piety and justice'). Blocked from the throne by the Phrecians, they rigged Izaro's Labyrinth so Chitus Perandus won; Cadiro looted the treasury before the fall. Descendants include Syndicate member Janus Perandus.

name: Phrecian dynasty
summary: Unbroken line of emperors descended from Alano Phrecia, who founded the line after killing the 'dark being' in 35 IC. It ran from Alano through Romira and Tyndarus to Izaro, who was childless.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "sections 'Reign of Alano Phrecia' to 'Reign of Izaro'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ancients", "locator": "Book 7: The Light of Phrecia"}]

name: Precursors
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "further before the Vaal than the Vaal are before the present", "story_order": null}
summary: Technologically superior ancient civilisation that wholly predates the Winter of the World; mastered corruption, built the Towers (terraforming), the Precursor Weapon and the Arbiter of Ash, then triggered cataclysms of fire, eruptions and sky-impacts. Pictographs read 'Death lies within'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > Precursor civilization"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 1"}]

name: Primeval Civilization ("Proto-Vaal")
summary: Ancient civilisation preceding the Vaal, unearthed in the Azurite Mine; the name "Proto-Vaal" is an internal term never used in-game and no link to the Vaal is established.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > Primeval civilization"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_primeval_civilization", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_primeval_civilization", "locator": "efn Proto-Vaal"}]

name: Purity Rebellion
summary: Coalition led by High Templar Voll of Thebrus against Chitus' gem-and-thaumaturgy 'thaumatocracy'. Its supporters included Victario, Ondar, Geofri, Kastov and Adus, with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh allies.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_purity_chronicles", "locator": "Book 1: Embers of Insurrection"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "section 'The Purity Rebellion'"}]

name: Redblades
summary: Human tribe descended from those who settled the Titans' volcanoes; they ritually sacrifice humans to the Molten One, possibly because a Titan destroyed an outpost of El'Abin.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > The Titans"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_molten_one", "locator": "God of the Redblades"}]

name: Remembrancers
summary: Kalguuran scribes who documented the explorations; the Prime Remembrancer's logbooks tell the expedition's fall.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "'===Society==='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "Culture; Society section"}]

name: Runefathers
summary: Aldur's chosen apprentices and artisans of runesmithing; forged the Triskelion Flame to reunite fractured Middengard.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "===The Triskelion Flame===: \"After Aldur had passed away, the Runefathers gathered to forge the Triskelion Flame.\""}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_aldur", "locator": "Aldur's death and the Runefathers"}]

name: Order of the Templar
summary: Theocratic order led by a High Templar that worships Innocence. Within the Eternal Empire it produced figures such as High Templars Andronicus and Voll; after the Cataclysm it governed the unaffected island of Oriath as the Templar Theocracy, with Dominus and Avarius as its PoE1-era High Templars.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "'Lore' section"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Oriath' and 'Lycia, the Heretic' sections"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "intro and section 'Lore'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_dominus", "locator": "Lore"}]

name: The Unblinking Eye
summary: Mysterious group associated with the Templars involved in notable events in Wraeclast's history.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_unblinking_eye", "locator": "lead"}]

name: The Three Sisters
summary: Cross-cultural myth of the sun, moon and earth sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and ended the Winter of the World; named differently by Eternals, Maraketh, Karui, Azmeri and the Wildwood Draiocht (Catha, Mhacha, Morrigan).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_three_sisters", "locator": "intro and culture list"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_three_sisters", "locator": "lead"}]

name: Trarthans
summary: People of Trarthus descended from Eternal Empire exiles and slaves, led by four Great Houses.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_trarthus", "locator": "intro"}]

name: The Twilight Order
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "Hidden for centuries; active ~20 years after the end of PoE1 (PoE1 present is ~1620 IC)", "story_order": null}
summary: Secret order, concealed for countless centuries, that rebuilt Oriath while the world believed it abandoned. It aims to free mankind from the 'tyranny of the gods' and build a god-free 'Utopia'; behind the scenes it is plotting to create a new Beast and trigger another Cataclysm. Led by the Countess (Oriana).

name: The Vaal
summary: Oldest identified civilisation of Wraeclast and in its heyday its most powerful nation; first known users of virtue gems, practitioners of mass blood sacrifice and slavery. All but 3,126 died in the Vaal Cataclysm; survivors assimilated into the Azmeri.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_vaal_oversoul", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest log 'Speak to Alva'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "lead + History"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Vaal'"}]

name: The Royal Architects of Atzoatl
summary: Group of Vaal architects serving Atziri who built the Temple; Incursion has Vaal Architect mini-bosses. PoE2 Medallion flavour names Architects of the Guild, Vault, Destruction, Hoard, Forge and Nexus and associates Quipolatl, Puhuarte, Juatalotli, Hayoxi, Estazunti with them.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "Figures"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_atziri_s_temple", "locator": "Medallions table"}]

name: Vaal survivors / Savage tribes heirs
summary: The 3,126 survivors who merged into Azmeri tribes; later Azmeri/Karui cultures inherit Vaal remnants. Descendants of Vaal blood persist (e.g. Alva Valai; the Cuachic).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "The Vaal Cataclysm"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Doryani: 'a living descendant of our people'"}]

name: Watchers of Decay
summary: Ancient organisation of parents founded when a nameless god told an Azmeri mother whose child was stolen about the Elder. They forged Starforge to subdue it by separating form and spirit. Their Map Device (Book of Memories p9) later became the Atlas device. Associated with the Order of the Djinn on the wiki; membership of Egrin/Qianga/Betucia is unclear.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Watchers of Decay"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_watchers_of_decay", "locator": "lead"}]

name: Abyss league
summary: Abyss league Launched 2017-12-08 (version 3.1.0). Abysses are cracks and pits spawning monsters; introduces abyss jewels, Stygian Vises, Abyssal Depths and Abyssal Liches.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_abyss_league", "locator": "lead paragraph (release 2017-12-08, v3.1.0)"}]

name: Ancestor league (Trial of the Ancestors)
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.22.0 (18 Aug - 5 Dec 2023): Exiles use Silver Coins to enter the Karui afterlife and field a team of Karui warriors in the Trial of the Ancestors tournament against fallen chieftains, under Hinekora.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_ancestor_league", "locator": "infobox + '==League mechanic=='"}]

name: Breach league
summary: Breach league Launched 2016-12-02 (version 2.5.0). Breaches open parallel realms of otherworldly monsters; splinters form Breachstones to challenge the five Breachlords in their domains.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_breach_league", "locator": "lead paragraph (release 2016-12-02, v2.5.0)"}]

name: Delirium league
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "3.10.0 'Path of Exile: Delirium', 2020-03-13 to 2020-06-15", "story_order": null}
summary: Challenge league in which Mirrors of Delirium in each area release a spreading fog of madness; leads to the Simulacrum and Cluster Jewels.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_delirium_league", "locator": "lead paragraph and 'League mechanic' section"}]

name: Expedition league
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "3.15.0 'Path of Exile: Expedition', 2021-07-23 to 2021-10-18", "story_order": null}
summary: Challenge league introducing four Kalguuran expedition NPCs (Gwennen, Tujen, Rog, Dannig) who excavate the lost settlements of their ancestors with explosives. The Kalguur are referenced again in Settlers (Kingsmarch) and in PoE2.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_expedition_league", "locator": "lead paragraph and 'League mechanic' section"}]

name: Keepers of the Flame league
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.27.0 (31 Oct 2025 - 2 Mar 2026): the Exile works with Ailith to repel Hiveborn invading via stabilised Breach connections and grows the Genesis Tree; Breach joined the core game in 3.28.0.

summary: PoE2 Early Access update 0.2.0 (launched 2025-04-04) and its temporary league. It added Azmeri wisps, rogue exiles and idols to the core game; not officially a full league.

summary: Delirium hub on the 0.5 Atlas, south-west of the starting point.

name: Wraeclast
summary: The continent on which the Exile's story takes place; PoE2 is set on (and expands) Wraeclast, while Oriath is another continent seen in PoE1.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro and Prehistory"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_wraeclast", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro; section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_1", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_6", "locator": "returns to Wraeclast"}]

name: Ziggurat Encampment
summary: Treasure hunter camp built atop a ziggurat in a lake; unknowingly sits on the time gateway. Town hub of PoE2 Act 3.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest logs 'Explore Ziggurat Encampment'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "quest log"}]

name: Ziggurat Refuge
summary: Where the Exile unintentionally ends up instead of Oriath; Doryani's Ziggurat above Precursor leylines holds the Waygate/Map Device.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_siege_of_oriath", "locator": "Quest Complete"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Speak to Doryani: leylines, Waygate"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Take a Waystone from Doryani in The Ziggurat Refuge"}]

name: Ancient Etchings (Kalandra)
summary: Series of Ancient Etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra herself, recounting her entrapment, scorn for gods (Etching V: a conversation with someone implied to be Sin), and the Order of the Djinn's failed rescue (Etching VI).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore > Ancient Etchings"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > The Lake of Kalandra footnotes"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore: Ancient Etchings"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Ancient Etchings entry (found throughout the Lake)"}]

name: The First Edict
summary: Unexplained so far. Tecrod, hunting for the Edicts, is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity with 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'; on completing the Epilogue quest Legacy of the Precursors the log reads 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.' Its contents are not described in sources read; 'ordain' implies it is something that can be enacted or activated, and the Origin Tower / Origin Core are the setting.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tecrod", "locator": "Lore: 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Quest Complete: 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tecrod", "locator": "Lore: Tecrod 'hunting for the Edicts'"}]

name: The Fourth Edict
summary: Mystery edict. In Legacy of the Precursors (0.5.0) the quest-log step 'Investigate the Fourth Edict' follows the defeat of the Arbiter of Ash; its contents are not revealed in the verified sources.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest step 102 'Investigate the Fourth Edict'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ezomytes", "locator": "The Great Fire: 'likely caused by the Fourth Edict, a contingency created by the Precursors to purge Wraeclast in flames'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_arbiter_of_ash", "locator": "quote 'The Fourth Edict beckons' (flaming orb attack) - reported via search result, unverified locally"}, {"source_id": "src_web_quora_fourth_edict", "locator": "fan answer: fourth edict = flame seed (speculation)"}]

name: The Second Edict
summary: Never shown directly. Only Doryani's speculation, after the Third Edict is revealed: 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict... Why would any civilisation intentionally create the Seed of Corruption?'
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict...'"}]

name: The Third Edict
summary: Precursor edict whose instrument is the Weapon. After the Hooded One reforges it, the inscription reads 'The instrument of the Third Edict'; the Weapon was 'designed for the sole purpose of cleansing Corruption... and destroying the Beast'. Revealed in Act 4 (0.3.0, whose update bears the name 'The Third Edict'). The Hooded One's wording ('that third mural') implies the edicts are murals he had seen in the Excavated Site.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural. The forging revealed an inscription. The symbols declare it The instrument of the Third Edict.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act", "locator": "Version history 0.3.0: 'The instrument of the Third Edict. Journey to Kingsmarch...'"}]

name: Emperor's Warning
summary: Notice at The Prisoner's arena: 'By the order of Emperor Izaro... The prisoner within is beyond death.' signed Emperor Chitus Perandus.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Emperor's Warning"}]

name: Feverish Writings (Niko)
summary: Letter by Niko ('Your master, Niko') in the Doomed Mine on the Isle of Kin, urging miners to gather sulphite while a blind beast whispers in the dark. Continues PoE1's Niko (Delve) into PoE2.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Feverish Writings"}]

name: Count Geonor's Edicts (Ogham decrees)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "~20 years after PoE1, Ogham, Act 1", "story_order": null}
summary: Notices posted across Ogham by Count Geonor declaring all crimes punishable by hanging, bodies thrown into a pit beneath his manor; a 'notice of criminality' is found near Clearfell. Not Precursor edicts; the executions fed the Beast seed/creature in the manor cage.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_yt_4UKJmVK7Iv4", "locator": "[0:25]-[0:41] 'The count's edicts posted throughout the island declared that all crimes were now punishable by hanging'; [4:25]-[4:36]"}]

name: Geonor's Journal
summary: Environmental lore in Ogham Manor: Geonor writes that Oriana 'assures me, we can right some of the wrongs of the past' and promises a way forward for Ogham, showing how the Countess recruited him.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Geonor's Journal (Ogham Manor)"}]

name: Letters from Chitus
summary: Three letters from Chitus to Cadiro (1316-1318 IC) planning to win Izaro's Labyrinth. Released as physical GGG merchandise.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_letters_from_chitus", "locator": "Transcripts"}]

name: Letters of Exile
summary: Environmental lore object in Lioneye's Watch: court papers nailed to stakes that give the sentences of named exiles (1597-1599 IC) in the formula 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. Added in version 0.10.8. Distinct from text_letters_from_chitus (Chitus's letters to Cadiro) and text_vaal_letters (Vaal victims' letters).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_letters_of_exile", "locator": "intro: 'Letters of Exile is an environmental lore object found in Lioneye's Watch.'; section '==Format==' sentencing formula; version history 0.10.8"}]

name: The Lord's Labyrinth (gamebook)
summary: An official GGG gamebook (2019) that retells the Lord's Labyrinth from Weylin's perspective. The PoE Wiki reports repeated inconsistencies with in-game sources, so it is generally not treated as canon.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_book_the_lords_labyrinth_gamebook", "locator": "gamebook forum post, 28 Oct 2019 (cited in History of Wraeclast, 'The Lord's Labyrinth')"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' (gamebook note: generally not canon)"}]

name: Lycia's relics
summary: Forbidden Sanctum relics revealing the Original Sin and Innocence's ascension.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "'Original Sin'"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_7QuY96FyhG4", "locator": "[10:13] origins of Innocence"}]

name: Path of Exile: Origins
summary: Official comic recounting Victario, the Karui Way, the Chamber of Sins and Chitus' death.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_book_poe_origins", "locator": "Issues 1-4"}]

name: Path of Exile: Origins (comic)
summary: A four-issue official comic by Grinding Gear Games and Dynamite Entertainment, told from Victario's perspective. Digital issues ran from July 2014 to April 2015; the paperback was published by Dynamite in June 2015. It centres on the Purity Rebellion and events leading up to the Cataclysm.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_book_path_of_exile_origins", "locator": "'Publication' section (issue table) and intro: written by Edwin McRae and Royal McGraw, illustrated by Carlos Rodriguez"}]

name: Precursor Edicts
summary: Vague Precursor murals depicting the Beast (or a precursor of it) and possibly instructions for containing it. The corpus separately says Sin later created the Beast from a Precursor Seed of Corruption; any reading that the Beast predates the gods is interpretation.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 1"}]

name: The Purity Chronicles
summary: Six-book chronicle by Garivaldi in the Library of Sarn (Act 3 area) on the Purity Rebellion.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_purity_chronicles", "locator": "Books 1-6"}]

name: Memory Fragments of the Shaper
summary: Seven in-game diary entries (Home, Intrigue, Wonder, Dream, Nightmare, Grief, Awakening) in which Valdo describes the golden device, dreams, Zana's capture and resolving to 'forge a world anew'. Partly superseded by the Book of Memories retcon.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_shaper_quest", "locator": "Memory Fragments section"}]

name: Chamber of Innocence stained glass windows
summary: Templar propaganda in Oriath depicting Innocence as pure and Sin as deceitful twin; later contradicted by Lycia.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "'Stained glass windows'"}]

name: Tavakai's Declaration
summary: In-game note found in Ngakanu: Tavakai declares the 'era of the Mighty', that the last Ngakuramakoi's body will become the new world and that 'The End of Time has come'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Tavakai's Declaration"}]

name: The Ancients (Trinian)
summary: In-game history by Trinian in the Library of Sarn (PoE1 Act 3), Books 1-5 on Atziri, Zerphi, Doryani, the Azmeri and the Fall.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "citations of Trinian"}]

name: Architects' notes in Atziri's Temple
summary: Environmental texts in Atziri's Temple: 'The Perfect Design' (Architect's living-machine temple, expecting Doryani's proxies to try to stop 'Atziri's Ascension'), 'Disloyalty' (an Architect suspects Doryani is moving against the Queen over the Red Communion) and 'The Forever Queen' (Atziri names a critic her personal Architect).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "'The Perfect Design', 'Disloyalty', 'The Forever Queen'"}]

name: Vaal Letters
summary: Twelve readable letters by victims and subjects of Atziri's regime, documenting sacrifice and dissent.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_vaal_letter", "locator": "page"}]

name: Victario's Writings
summary: Four environmental lore texts in The Library, written as anecdotes and allegory by the poet Victario of Sarn: Kalisa Maas and the Virtue gem that shatters glass; the Blackest Monkey parable; Slaves of Virtue, on shackled workers who mine gems for the Eternal citizens while Malachai abuses them; and A Friend in Need, on the musician Lorenzi who has a gem implanted in his hand.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_victario_s_writings", "locator": "section headings 'Volume 1: Kalisa Maas', 'Volume 2: The Blackest Monkey', 'Volume 3: Slaves of Virtue' (mentions Malachai and Highgate), 'Volume 4: A Friend in Need' (Lorenzi and Malachai's gem implant); each signed 'Victario of Sarn'"}]

name: Voll's Confession
summary: Voll's confession that he trusted the most corrupt of men.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_voll_emperor_of_purity", "locator": "Lore: The Cataclysm"}]
